findings.reason: a §3 node dispatched against a §1-only table has no artifact for the multi-group family condition and must either block or re-derive a lead ruling it does not own.
findings.text: §3's done-when refuses a cut "when a family of the group has a member in another group and the ruling recorded in §2 does not list that family as an exception or name the two groups as cut together", so §3 consumes §2's recorded family-ruling list, yet the dependency declaration gives s3 only `sn-audited-group-release#s1`; §2 states in its own done-when that its ruling is "the list the release bar reads"

findings.reason: the worker cannot tell which total the census must reconcile to, so the sum check either fails on exactly the 23 names the section reports or is silently reinterpreted, and either way the reconciliation the section exists to prove is not fixed.
findings.text: §2's own census reads 3,266 live names carrying a physics domain and 23 carrying none, while the done-when asserts "the per-group counts sum to the live total"; the 29 groups partition only the 3,266, so the invariant is false against the live total the section's figures imply (3,289) and true only against the domain-carrying subset

findings.reason: with no planted three-member shared cause whose member-by-member repair must be refused, the node cannot show its routing fires, so its correct behaviour and its complete absence are the same evidence.
findings.text: §4 requires that "a cause shared by three or more defective members is reported as a pipeline defect and is not repaired member by member" and that "none is edited in place outside the pipeline's own write paths", but unlike §2 ("a recorded run shows the census counting …") and §3 ("a recorded run shows each refusal on a group planted with that one fault") the section declares no planted case and no recorded run for either guard; a run that reports zero shared causes and repairs every member individually satisfies the done-when as written

findings.reason: one verdict cannot close both, so a coordinator accepting this node's result cannot state which of the two it is accepting, and a split is the only way to close either on its own evidence.
findings.text: §4 delivers two independently closable endpoints in one node: the first group brought to the §3 bar and cut as a release candidate, and the two-arm regeneration/agent-proposal comparison, whose outcome the section explicitly permits to be inconclusive ("where the counts are too small to say"); the cut can close while the comparison reports nothing usable, and the comparison can be conclusive while the cut fails at the bar
